about: 20 cases for the Phase-0 survey: 13 answers with an error a checker should flag, 7 correct answers it must pass. 'origin' says whether the error happened with a real model (handoff section 5) or is an everyday rewrite of one. Trace cases are given to text-only tools as passages, one per tool call (see run_survey.render_passages).

cases.origin: everyday rewrite of: quoted a number no passage contains
cases.why: 42.1 is not in the source (it says 41.2)
cases.question: What was Acme's revenue in Q3?

sources.text: Acme's revenue for the third quarter was $41.2 million, up 8% from the second quarter.

cases.answer: Acme's Q3 revenue was $42.1 million, up 8% from Q2 [S1].

cases.origin: control: rounding
cases.why: 24 and 14 are 23.7 and 14.2 rounded, and the answer says 'about'
cases.question: How warm will Pune be on Thursday?

sources.text: Forecast for Pune on Thursday: high 23.7 °C, low 14.2 °C, chance of rain 10%.

cases.answer: Thursday in Pune: a high of about 24 °C and a low of about 14 °C, with a 10% chance of rain [S1].

cases.origin: control: thousands separator, a rate written as a percentage
cases.question: What does the loan cost per month and in total?

sources.text: Loan quote: principal 11020.78 USD, annual rate 0.07, term 36 months, monthly payment 340.29 USD, total repaid 12250.43 USD.

cases.answer: At 7% over 36 months you pay 340.29 USD a month and 12,250.43 USD in total [S1].

cases.origin: real error (DeepSeek V4 Flash, project 1, 2026-11-04)
cases.why: the tool gave concurrence 0.55; 0.7 is the Werner weight, quoted as the concurrence
cases.question: Apply global depolarizing noise with p = 0.3 to phi+. What is its concurrence?
cases.answer: Global depolarizing noise with p = 0.3 turns phi+ into a Werner state with p_W = 0.7, so concurrence = 0.7.

cases.origin: everyday rewrite of the value-to-field error
cases.why: rebounds and assists are swapped: every number is in the result, two of them attached to the wrong field
cases.question: How did Jordan Reyes play last night?
cases.answer: Jordan Reyes scored 27 points with 7 rebounds and 11 assists in 34 minutes.

cases.origin: everyday rewrite of the value-to-field error
cases.why: the chance of rain is 70; 4 is the low temperature
cases.question: What will the weather be like in Oslo tomorrow?
cases.answer: Tomorrow in Oslo: a high of 9 °C, wind of 18 km/h and a 4% chance of rain.

cases.origin: control
cases.why: both values are attached to the right fields
cases.question: What do I pay per month and in total for the 3-year loan at 7%?
cases.answer: Over 3 years at 7% you pay 340.29 a month and 12,250.43 in total.

cases.origin: real error (project 1 Space, found by the reviewer Kreout)
cases.why: the question asks for p = 0.3 but the tool ran with p = 0.03; the result is quoted faithfully, so every number is grounded
cases.question: Apply global depolarizing noise with p = 0.3 to phi+. What is its concurrence?
cases.answer: With global depolarizing noise of p = 0.3, the concurrence of phi+ falls to 0.955.

cases.origin: everyday rewrite of the Kreout case (handoff section 7)
cases.why: the question asks for 5 years but the tool was called with years=3
cases.question: What is the 5-year cost at 7% interest?
cases.answer: Over 5 years at 7% you pay 12,250 in total, 340.29 a month.

cases.origin: everyday rewrite of: two values swapped between two calls
cases.why: the amounts are swapped between the two calls: 73.60 EUR is 80 USD, 140.40 EUR is 120 GBP
cases.question: Convert 120 USD and 80 GBP to euros.
cases.answer: 120 USD is 73.60 EUR and 80 GBP is 140.40 EUR.

cases.origin: control: a real false positive of project 1 ('p = 0.3 and 0.1 respectively')
cases.why: global ran with 0.3 and local with 0.1, as asked
cases.question: Apply global and local depolarizing noise with p = 0.3 and 0.1 respectively to phi+, and compare the concurrences.
cases.answer: Global depolarizing noise with p = 0.3 leaves a concurrence of 0.55; local depolarizing noise with p = 0.1 on both photons leaves 0.715.

cases.origin: everyday rewrite of: a failed tool call reported as a result
cases.why: the only call failed, yet the answer reports a forecast
cases.question: What will the weather be like in Oslo tomorrow?
cases.answer: Tomorrow in Oslo: about 9 °C with a 70% chance of rain.

cases.origin: control: a failed call that was redone
cases.why: the first call failed, the retry succeeded, and the answer quotes the retry
cases.question: What will the weather be like in Oslo tomorrow?
cases.answer: Tomorrow in Oslo: a high of 9 °C with a 70% chance of rain.

cases.origin: everyday case: a claim about a tool that was never called
cases.why: the answer says it searched the web; no search tool was called
cases.question: Is the MX-200 battery still under warranty after 3 years?
cases.answer: I searched the web and found that the MX-200 warranty is 2 years, so after 3 years it has expired.

cases.origin: real error type (project 2: a quote with changed words)
cases.why: the source says 'does not guarantee', the quote says 'does not ensure'
cases.question: What is the drawback of linear inversion?

sources.text: Linear inversion does not guarantee that the reconstructed matrix is positive.

cases.answer: The source warns that linear inversion "does not ensure that the reconstructed matrix is positive" [S1].
cases.flag_span: does not ensure that the reconstructed matrix is positive

cases.origin: everyday rewrite of: a quote from another passage than the one cited
cases.why: the quote is in S2, but the answer cites S1
cases.question: How does the X200 router get firmware updates?

sources.text: The X200 router supports Wi-Fi 6 and has four gigabit ports.
Firmware updates are installed automatically every night at 3 a.m.

cases.answer: According to the manual, "firmware updates are installed automatically every night" [S1].
cases.flag_span: firmware updates are installed automatically every night

cases.origin: control: typographic differences only
cases.why: straight vs curly quote marks, '3 %' vs '3%': the same wording
cases.question: How large is the effect?

sources.text: The study's authors call the effect “small but robust” — about 3% of the variance.

cases.answer: The authors call the effect "small but robust", about 3 % of the variance [S1].

cases.origin: real wording (project 1: 'Let me report the tool's numbers', 'Wait, let me check')
cases.why: the model's thinking aloud is left in the answer; the numbers themselves are right
cases.question: What do I pay per month and in total for the 3-year loan at 7%?
cases.answer: Let me report the tool's numbers: the total is 12,250.43. Wait, let me check: the monthly payment is 340.29.

cases.origin: real error type (project 2: 'the passages do not say X', then X from them)
cases.why: the answer says the sources do not give the warranty, then gives it from them
cases.question: How long is the warranty?

sources.text: The warranty period is two years from the date of purchase.

cases.answer: The passages do not say how long the warranty lasts. The warranty lasts two years from the date of purchase [S1].
cases.flag_span: The passages do not say how long the warranty lasts.

cases.origin: control: a TRUE sentence project 1 once removed ('takes a bigger toll')
cases.why: local noise on both photons leaves concurrence 0.235, global 0.55: local does take the bigger toll
cases.question: Apply local depolarizing noise to both photons and global depolarizing noise, each with p = 0.3, to phi+. Which destroys more entanglement?
cases.answer: Local noise takes a bigger toll on entanglement: the concurrence falls to 0.235, against 0.55 under global noise.
